1Jephthah the Gileadite was a mighty man of valor, and he was the son of a prostitute. Gilead was the father of Jephthah.

2Gilead's wife also bore him sons, and when his wife's sons grew up, they drove Jephthah out and said to him, "You shall not inherit in our father's house, for you are the son of another woman."

3So Jephthah fled from his brothers and lived in the land of Tob. Worthless men gathered around Jephthah and went out raiding with him.

4And it came to pass after a time that the sons of Ammon made war against Israel.

5When the sons of Ammon made war against Israel, the elders of Gilead went to bring Jephthah from the land of Tob.

6They said to Jephthah, "Come and be our commander, so that we may fight against the sons of Ammon."

7Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "Did you not hate me and drive me out of my father's house? Why have you come to me now, when you are in distress?"

8The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "That is why we have turned to you now: come with us and fight against the sons of Ammon, and you shall be our head, over all the inhabitants of Gilead."

9Jephthah said to the elders of Gilead, "If you bring me back to fight against the sons of Ammon, and the LORD gives them over to me, I will be your head."

10The elders of Gilead said to Jephthah, "The LORD will be the witness between us; we will surely do as you have said."

11So Jephthah went with the elders of Gilead, and the people made him head and commander over them. Jephthah spoke all his words before the LORD at Mizpah.

Jephthah's Message to Ammon

12Jephthah sent messengers to the king of the sons of Ammon, saying, "What do you have against me, that you have come to me to fight against my land?"

13The king of the sons of Ammon said to Jephthah's messengers, "Because Israel took my land when they came up from Egypt, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and to the Jordan. And now give those lands back peaceably."

14Jephthah sent messengers again to the king of the sons of Ammon,

15and said to him, "Thus says Jephthah: Israel did not take the land of Moab or the land of the sons of Ammon.

16When they came up from Egypt, Israel went through the wilderness to the Sea of Reeds and came to Kadesh.

17Israel sent messengers to the king of Edom, saying, 'Please let me pass through your land,' but the king of Edom would not listen. They sent also to the king of Moab, but he would not consent. So Israel stayed at Kadesh.

18Then they went through the wilderness and went around the land of Edom and the land of Moab, and came to the east side of the land of Moab, and camped beyond the Arnon. They did not enter the territory of Moab, for the Arnon was the border of Moab.

19Israel sent messengers to Sihon king of the Amorites, king of Heshbon, and Israel said to him, 'Please let us pass through your land to our place.'

20But Sihon did not trust Israel to pass through his territory. Sihon gathered all his people, camped at Jahaz and fought with Israel.

21The LORD, the God of Israel, gave Sihon and all his people into the hand of Israel, and they struck them. So Israel took possession of all the land of the Amorites, the inhabitants of that land.

22They took possession of all the territory of the Amorites, from the Arnon to the Jabbok and from the wilderness to the Jordan.

23And now the LORD, the God of Israel, has driven out the Amorites before His people Israel, and should you take possession of it?

24Will you not possess what Chemosh your god gives you to possess? So we will possess all that the LORD our God has driven out before us.

25And now, are you any better than Balak son of Zippor, king of Moab? Did he ever strive with Israel, or did he ever fight against them?

26While Israel lived in Heshbon and its towns, in Aroer and its towns, and in all the cities along the Arnon, three hundred years, why did you not recover them within that time?

27I have not sinned against you, but you are doing me wrong by making war on me. May the LORD, the Judge, judge today between the sons of Israel and the sons of Ammon."

28But the king of the sons of Ammon did not listen to the words that Jephthah sent him.

The Vow

29The Spirit of the LORD came upon Jephthah, and he passed through Gilead and Manasseh, passed through Mizpah of Gilead, and from Mizpah of Gilead he passed on to the sons of Ammon.

30Jephthah made a vow to the LORD and said, "If You will give the sons of Ammon into my hand,

31then whoever comes out of the doors of my house to meet me when I return in peace from the sons of Ammon shall be the LORD's, and I will offer him up as a burnt offering."

32So Jephthah crossed over to the sons of Ammon to fight against them, and the LORD gave them into his hand.

33He struck them from Aroer to the approach of Minnith, twenty cities, and as far as Abel-keramim, a very great defeat. So the sons of Ammon were subdued before the sons of Israel.

Jephthah's Daughter

34Then Jephthah came to his home at Mizpah, and his daughter came out to meet him with tambourines and with dancing. She was his only child; besides her he had neither son nor daughter.

35And it came to pass, when he saw her, that he tore his clothes and said, "Alas, my daughter! You have brought me very low, and you have become the one who troubles me. I have opened my mouth to the LORD, and I cannot take it back."

36She said to him, "My father, you have opened your mouth to the LORD. Do to me as it came out of your mouth, now that the LORD has taken vengeance for you on your enemies, the sons of Ammon."

37She said to her father, "Let this be done for me: let me alone two months, so that I may go and go down on the mountains and weep for my virginity, I and my companions."

38He said, "Go." He sent her away for two months, and she went with her companions and wept for her virginity on the mountains.

39And it came to pass at the end of two months that she returned to her father, and he did to her his vow that he had vowed. She had never known a man. It became a custom in Israel:

40year by year the daughters of Israel would go to tell of the daughter of Jephthah the Gileadite, four days in the year.

Notes

  • v1 "the son of a prostitute" — ben ishah zonah, the words used of Rahab, ishah zonah (Joshua 2:1). Like Abimelech, the son of a slave woman (9:18), Jephthah is a son from outside the marriage, and his brothers turn him out.

  • vv6–11 "commander… head" — the elders first offer qatsin, commander for the war. Jephthah reminds them how they treated him, and the offer rises to rosh, head over all Gilead, for life. He takes both, and has the bargain spoken before the LORD at Mizpah.

  • vv15–27 Jephthah's history — the message follows Numbers 20:14–21 and 21:21–31 closely: Edom's refusal, the road around Moab, Sihon at Jahaz, the land from the Arnon to the Jabbok.

  • v24 "Chemosh your god" — Chemosh is the god of Moab (people of Chemosh, Numbers 21:29); the Ammonite god is Milcom (1 Kings 11:5). The land in dispute had been Moab's before Sihon took it (Numbers 21:26), and Jephthah answers in Moab's terms.

  • v27 "the LORD, the Judge" — ha-shofet, the only time in the book the title is given to God. The judges of Israel are named for what He does.

  • v31 "whoever comes out… to meet me" — ha-yotse asher yetse, the one who comes out, masculine, which in Hebrew covers a person or an animal. To meet me, liqrati, is used of people coming out to greet someone. The Hebrew allows both readings.

  • v34 "with tambourines and with dancing… his only child" — the words of Exodus 15:20, where Miriam and the women go out after the victory at the sea. His only child is yechidah, the word God used of Isaac in Genesis 22:2. Isaac was spared; this story has no ram.

  • v35 "the one who troubles me" — be-okhrai, from akhar, the word Joshua spoke to Achan: Why have you brought trouble on us? (Joshua 7:25). Jephthah blames his daughter for his own words.

  • v36 "Do to me as it came out of your mouth" — yatsa, the verb of the vow: whoever comes out (v31). What came out of his mouth and who came out of his door are said with one word. Numbers 30:2 holds a man to everything that has come out of his mouth.

  • vv39–40 "he did to her his vow… to tell of the daughter of Jephthah" — the text does not describe the act, and says next that she had never known a man. To tell of, letannot, is the verb of 5:11, where Israel recounts the righteous acts of the LORD; here the daughters of Israel recount her. The Greek has to mourn.

chapters.title: Shibboleth, and Three Judges
chapters.html:
Judges 12

Shibboleth

1The men of Ephraim were called out, and they crossed over to Zaphon and said to Jephthah, "Why did you cross over to fight against the sons of Ammon and not call us to go with you? We will burn your house over you with fire."

2Jephthah said to them, "I and my people had a great quarrel with the sons of Ammon. I called you, and you did not save me from their hand.

3When I saw that you would not save me, I took my life in my hands and crossed over to the sons of Ammon, and the LORD gave them into my hand. Why then have you come up to me this day to fight against me?"

4Jephthah gathered all the men of Gilead and fought against Ephraim, and the men of Gilead struck Ephraim, because they had said, "You are fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites, in the middle of Ephraim and in the middle of Manasseh."

5The Gileadites seized the fords of the Jordan against Ephraim. And it would come to pass, whenever a fugitive of Ephraim said, "Let me cross over," that the men of Gilead would say to him, "Are you an Ephraimite?" When he said, "No,"

6they would say to him, "Then say 'Shibboleth.'" He would say "Sibboleth," for he could not pronounce it right. Then they would seize him and slaughter him at the fords of the Jordan. At that time forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell.

7Jephthah judged Israel six years. Then Jephthah the Gileadite died and was buried in one of the cities of Gilead.

Ibzan, Elon and Abdon

8After him Ibzan of Bethlehem judged Israel.

9He had thirty sons, and thirty daughters whom he gave in marriage outside his clan, and he brought in thirty daughters from outside for his sons. He judged Israel seven years.

10Ibzan died and was buried at Bethlehem.

11After him Elon the Zebulunite judged Israel. He judged Israel ten years.

12Elon the Zebulunite died and was buried at Aijalon in the land of Zebulun.

13After him Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite judged Israel.

14He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, who rode on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel eight years.

15Abdon son of Hillel the Pirathonite died and was buried at Pirathon in the land of Ephraim, in the hill country of the Amalekites.

Notes

  • vv1–3 Ephraim's complaint — the same complaint Ephraim made to Gideon (8:1). Gideon calmed them with a proverb; Jephthah answers with the facts and then with the sword. Zaphon is a town in the Jordan valley (Joshua 13:27); the word also means north, and the Greek reads it so.

  • v3 "I took my life in my hands" — va-asimah nafshi ve-khappi, I put my soul in my palm: held out, easy to lose.

  • v4 "You are fugitives of Ephraim, you Gileadites" — the insult is hard to read. Most take it as Ephraim's jeer that Gilead is made of runaways from Ephraim and Manasseh; the Hebrew gives only the words, and the Greek gives the same.

  • vv5–6 "Shibboleth… Sibboleth" — shibbolet means an ear of grain or a flowing stream. The meaning did not matter; the first sound did. The Ephraimites said s where Gilead said sh, and one letter decided who lived. English took shibboleth from this verse for any test word that betrays a group. The Greek, which could not show the difference, has Say "Stachys", ear of grain, and drops the second word.

  • v6 "forty-two thousand of Ephraim fell" — Israel's worst losses so far in the book come at the hand of Israel.

  • v7 "in one of the cities of Gilead" — the Hebrew has be-arei Gil'ad, in the cities of Gilead, a plural where one town is expected. The Greek reads in his city, in Gilead. The Greek also has sixty years where the Hebrew has six.

  • v9 "thirty sons, and thirty daughters" — Ibzan's children marry outside, ha-chutsah: a judge known for his marriage alliances, not his battles.

  • vv11–12 "Elon… Aijalon" — in Hebrew the two names are the same letters, Elon and Ayyalon. The judge is buried in the town that bears his name.

  • v15 "in the hill country of the Amalekites" — an old name for part of Ephraim's hill country; the Song of Deborah speaks of Ephraim whose root is in Amalek (5:14).

chapters.title: The Birth of Samson
chapters.html:
Judges 13

The Promise

1The sons of Israel again did evil in the eyes of the LORD, and the LORD gave them into the hand of the Philistines forty years.

2There was a certain man of Zorah, of the clan of the Danites, whose name was Manoah. His wife was barren and had borne no children.

3The messenger of the LORD appeared to the woman and said to her, "You are barren and have borne no children, but you shall conceive and bear a son.

4So now, be careful: do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean,

5for you are pregnant and will bear a son. No razor shall go up on his head, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb, and he shall begin to save Israel from the hand of the Philistines."

6The woman went and told her husband, "A man of God came to me, and his appearance was like the appearance of the messenger of God, very fearsome. I did not ask him where he was from, and he did not tell me his name.

7He said to me, 'You are pregnant and will bear a son. So now do not drink wine or strong drink, and do not eat anything unclean, for the boy shall be a Nazirite of God from the womb to the day of his death.'"

The Messenger Returns

8Manoah entreated the LORD and said, "Please, my Lord, let the man of God whom You sent come to us again and teach us what we are to do for the boy who will be born."

9God listened to the voice of Manoah, and the messenger of God came again to the woman as she was sitting in the field. But Manoah her husband was not with her.

10The woman ran quickly and told her husband, "The man who came to me the other day has appeared to me."

11Manoah rose and followed his wife. He came to the man and said to him, "Are you the man who spoke to the woman?" He said, "I am."

12Manoah said, "Now, when your words come true, what shall be the boy's way of life, and what shall he do?"

13The messenger of the LORD said to Manoah, "Let the woman be careful about all that I said to her.

14She shall not eat anything that comes from the grapevine, or drink wine or strong drink, or eat anything unclean. Let her keep all that I have commanded her."

The Offering

15Manoah said to the messenger of the LORD, "Please let us detain you and prepare a young goat for you."

16The messenger of the LORD said to Manoah, "If you detain me, I will not eat your food. But if you prepare a burnt offering, offer it to the LORD." For Manoah did not know that he was the messenger of the LORD.

17Manoah said to the messenger of the LORD, "What is your name, so that we may honor you when your words come true?"

18The messenger of the LORD said to him, "Why do you ask my name? It is wonderful."

19Manoah took the young goat with the grain offering and offered it on the rock to the LORD, and He worked a wonder while Manoah and his wife looked on.

20When the flame went up from the altar toward heaven, the messenger of the LORD went up in the flame of the altar, while Manoah and his wife looked on. They fell on their faces to the ground.

21The messenger of the LORD did not appear again to Manoah and his wife. Then Manoah knew that he was the messenger of the LORD.

22Manoah said to his wife, "We shall surely die, for we have seen God."

23His wife said to him, "If the LORD had meant to kill us, He would not have accepted a burnt offering and a grain offering from our hands, or shown us all these things, or let us hear such things now."

Samson

24The woman bore a son and called his name Samson. The boy grew, and the LORD blessed him.

25The Spirit of the LORD began to stir him in Mahaneh-dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

Notes

  • v1 "gave them into the hand of the Philistines forty years" — every earlier cycle with a named deliverer has the sons of Israel cry out before a deliverer is raised (3:9, 3:15, 4:3, 6:6, 10:10). Here there is no cry. The deliverer is announced before anyone asks.

  • v2 "His wife was barren" — the mother is never named, while Manoah is. She joins Sarai (Genesis 11:30), Rebekah (25:21) and Rachel (29:31), barren wives who are promised a son. Zorah and Eshtaol are towns of Dan (Joshua 19:41).

  • v5 "a Nazirite of God from the womb" — Numbers 6 lays down the Nazirite vow as one a man or woman takes for the days of a set period. Here it is not taken at all: it is laid on the child before birth, and v7 has it last to the day of his death. No razor shall go up on his head, morah, is the razor of Numbers 6:5, ta'ar, under another name; the Greek has iron. The mother carries the first part of the restriction for him (vv4, 7, 14).

  • v5 "he shall begin to save" — yachel lehoshia, he shall begin. The verse promises a start, not an end.

  • v14 "anything that comes from the grapevine" — the messenger's second speech is wider than his first: v4 forbids wine and strong drink; v14 adds every product of the vine, the law of Numbers 6:4, he shall eat nothing that is made from the grapevine. The messenger tells Manoah nothing new about the boy; he repeats what the woman already had (v13).

  • v18 "Why do you ask my name? It is wonderful." — lamah zeh tish'al lishmi, the same words the man at the ford speaks to Jacob in Genesis 32:29, and there too no name is given. Peli is from pele, wonder, a thing beyond understanding, the word in pele yo'ets, a title in Isaiah 9:5 (English 9:6). It can be read wonderful or beyond understanding; the Greek has thaumaston, wonderful.

  • v19 "He worked a wonder" — u-mafli la'asot, from the same root as peli. The sentence has no named subject; the closest is the LORD. The Greek reads differently, he set apart to do, and does not have a wonder here.

  • vv22–23 "We shall surely die… If the LORD had meant to kill us" — the fear of Gideon, who also thought he would die after seeing the messenger face to face (6:22–23). There the LORD answers you shall not die; here the woman answers, and she reasons from the offering: a God who meant to kill would not have accepted it. She is the one who understands the sign.

  • v24 "Samson" — Shimshon, built on shemesh, sun. The text gives the name and does not explain it.

  • v25 "began to stir him" — lefa'amo, from pa'am, to strike, to beat, the root of his spirit was beaten in Genesis 41:8. The Spirit does not fill Samson or clothe him (6:34); it beats at him. The Greek has began to go out with him. Mahaneh-dan, camp of Dan, gets its name in 18:12, from a camp of the Danites near Kiriath-jearim.

chapters.title: Samson's Wedding and the Riddle
chapters.html:
Judges 14

The Woman at Timnah

1Samson went down to Timnah and saw a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines.

2He came back up and told his father and mother, "I have seen a woman in Timnah, one of the daughters of the Philistines. So now get her for me as a wife."

3His father and mother said to him, "Is there no woman among the daughters of your brothers, or among all our people, that you must go and take a wife from the uncircumcised Philistines?" But Samson said to his father, "Get her for me, for she is right in my eyes."

4His father and mother did not know that it was from the LORD, for he was seeking an occasion against the Philistines. At that time the Philistines were ruling over Israel.

The Lion and the Honey

5Samson went down to Timnah with his father and mother, and they came to the vineyards of Timnah. A young lion came roaring at him.

6The Spirit of the LORD rushed on him, and he tore the lion in two as one tears a young goat, with nothing in his hand. But he did not tell his father or his mother what he had done.

7He went down and spoke to the woman, and she was right in Samson's eyes.

8After a time he returned to take her, and he turned aside to see the carcass of the lion. In the body of the lion was a swarm of bees and honey.

9He scraped the honey into his hands and went on, eating as he went. When he came to his father and mother, he gave some to them, and they ate. But he did not tell them that he had scraped the honey from the body of the lion.

The Riddle

10His father went down to the woman, and Samson held a feast there, for that is what young men used to do.

11When the people saw him, they brought thirty companions to be with him.

12Samson said to them, "Let me tell you a riddle. If you can explain it to me within the seven days of the feast and find it out, I will give you thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.

13But if you cannot explain it to me, you shall give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes." They said to him, "Tell us your riddle, and let us hear it."

14He said to them,

"Out of the eater came something to eat,
and out of the strong came something sweet."

For three days they could not explain the riddle.

15On the seventh day they said to Samson's wife, "Coax your husband to explain the riddle to us, or we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Did you invite us here to dispossess us?"

16Samson's wife wept over him and said, "You only hate me; you do not love me. You have set a riddle for the sons of my people, and you have not told me the answer." He said to her, "I have not even told my father or my mother. Shall I tell you?"

17She wept over him the seven days that the feast lasted. On the seventh day he told her, because she pressed him hard. Then she explained the riddle to the sons of her people.

18The men of the city said to him on the seventh day, before the sun went down,

"What is sweeter than honey?
What is stronger than a lion?"

He said to them,

"If you had not plowed with my heifer,
you would not have found out my riddle."

Ashkelon

19The Spirit of the LORD rushed on him, and he went down to Ashkelon and struck down thirty men of the town. He took their clothing and gave the changes of clothes to those who had explained the riddle. In hot anger he went up to his father's house.

20Samson's wife was given to his companion, who had been his friend.

Notes

  • v1 "Timnah" — a town on the Danite list (Joshua 19:43), down the valley from Zorah, where Samson's family lives.

  • v3 "she is right in my eyes" — hi yashrah be-einai. It is the phrase the book ends on: everyone did what was right in his own eyes (21:25; also 17:6). The boy set apart from the womb chooses his wife by his own eyes.

  • v4 "it was from the LORD… an occasion" — to'anah, found only here. It is a pretext or an occasion, and it is the LORD who is seeking it. The Greek has vengeance. The parents are not told, and the text names the LORD as the cause without saying how.

  • v6 "rushed on him" — va-titslach alav, the verb of the LORD's Spirit coming on Saul in 1 Samuel 10:6, will rush upon you. It is used of Samson again in v19 and at 15:14. The Greek has leapt on him. With nothing in his hand is the point: the strength is not his own.

  • vv8–10 the carcass, the honey, the feast — Numbers 6:6 says a Nazirite shall not go near a dead body, and 13:4 forbade the mother wine; here Samson turns aside to a carcass, eats from it, and holds a mishteh, a drinking feast, from shatah, to drink. The chapter never says that any of this breaks his vow, and it never says that it does not. Twice he keeps it from his parents (vv6, 9).

  • v15 "On the seventh day" — the Hebrew has the men come on the seventh day, but v14 says they failed for three days, and v17 says the wife wept for all seven days of the feast. The Greek has on the fourth day, which fits both. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • v18 "before the sun went down" — be-terem yavo ha-charsah. Charsah is found only here; cheres is a rare word for the sun (Job 9:7), and the traditional reading is sunset. The Greek has before the sun rose. The sentence gives the answer just before the time is up.

  • v18 "If you had not plowed with my heifer" — a saying found only here: the men have plowed with his wife.

  • v19 "Ashkelon" — a Philistine city here, as Gaza is in 16:1, though 1:18 says Judah took both. The Greek of 1:18 says Judah did not inherit them.

  • v20 "his companion, who had been his friend" — le-mereehu asher ra'ah lo, his companion who had befriended him. The Greek has one of his friends whom he had befriended.

chapters.title: The Foxes, and the Jawbone
chapters.html:
Judges 15

The Foxes

1After a time, in the days of the wheat harvest, Samson visited his wife with a young goat. He said, "I will go in to my wife in her room." But her father would not let him go in.

2Her father said, "I was sure that you hated her, so I gave her to your companion. Is not her younger sister better than she? Please, let her be yours instead."

3Samson said to them, "This time I am blameless toward the Philistines when I do them harm."

4Samson went and caught three hundred foxes. He took torches, turned the foxes tail to tail, and put one torch between each pair of tails.

5He set fire to the torches and let the foxes go into the standing grain of the Philistines. He burned up the stacked grain and the standing grain, and the vineyards and olive groves.

6The Philistines said, "Who did this?" They said, "Samson, the son-in-law of the Timnite, because he took his wife and gave her to his companion." So the Philistines went up and burned her and her father with fire.

7Samson said to them, "If you act like this, I will take revenge on you, and after that I will stop."

8He struck them down with a great slaughter. Then he went down and stayed in the cleft of the rock of Etam.

Lehi

9The Philistines went up and camped in Judah and spread out at Lehi.

10The men of Judah said, "Why have you come up against us?" They said, "We have come up to bind Samson, to do to him as he did to us."

11Three thousand men of Judah went down to the cleft of the rock of Etam and said to Samson, "Do you not know that the Philistines rule over us? What is this you have done to us?" He said to them, "As they did to me, so I have done to them."

12They said to him, "We have come down to bind you and give you into the hand of the Philistines." Samson said to them, "Swear to me that you will not attack me yourselves."

13They said to him, "No. We will only bind you and give you into their hand, but we will not kill you." They bound him with two new ropes and brought him up from the rock.

14When he came to Lehi, the Philistines shouted as they met him. Then the Spirit of the LORD rushed on him, and the ropes on his arms became like flax that has caught fire, and the bonds melted off his hands.

15He found a fresh jawbone of a donkey, put out his hand, took it, and struck a thousand men with it.

16Samson said,

"With the jawbone of a donkey, heap upon heap!
With the jawbone of a donkey I have struck down a thousand men."

17When he had finished speaking, he threw the jawbone from his hand, and he called that place Ramath-lehi.

The Spring at Lehi

18He was very thirsty and called on the LORD and said, "You have given this great deliverance into the hand of Your servant, and now shall I die of thirst and fall into the hand of the uncircumcised?"

19God split open the hollow place that is at Lehi, and water came out of it. He drank, and his spirit returned, and he revived. So he called its name En-hakkore, which is at Lehi to this day.

20He judged Israel in the days of the Philistines twenty years.

Notes

  • v4 "three hundred foxes" — shu'alim, the word for both fox and jackal; translators divide over which is meant. The Greek has foxes. The burning falls in the days of the wheat harvest (v1), when the grain stands dry.

  • v6 "burned her and her father with fire" — the threat of the thirty companions in 14:15: we will burn you and your father's house with fire. Samson's wife dies of the very thing she gave up his riddle to escape.

  • v8 "a great slaughter" — the Hebrew is shoq al yarekh, leg on thigh, an expression found only here. It is thought to describe a thorough, merciless blow, but nothing else in the Bible fixes its sense. The Greek is literal, leg upon thigh.

  • v14 "the Spirit of the LORD rushed on him" — the third time (14:6, 14:19). Each of the three is followed at once by an act of violence.

  • v15 "a fresh jawbone" — lechi chamor teriyyah. Teriyyah is moist, fresh, the word for an open wound in Isaiah 1:6. The word marks a bone not yet dried out.

  • v16 "heap upon heap" — chamor chamorattayim. Chamor is a donkey, and chomer is a heap; the line puns on the weapon. The same heap word describes the frogs in Exodus 8:14, heap after heap. The Greek reads wiping out, I wiped them out, taking the word from another root.

  • v17 "Ramath-lehi" — ramat lechi, the height of the jawbone, or, from ramah, to throw, the throwing of the jawbone. The text gives the name at the moment he throws it.

  • v18 "this great deliverance" — ha-teshu'ah ha-gedolah, from yasha, to save, the verb the messenger used of him in 13:5, he shall begin to save Israel. The first deliverance is the one he now calls great, and he asks for water.

  • v19 "the hollow place" — ha-maktesh, found again in Zephaniah 1:11 as the name of a district in Jerusalem, and in Proverbs 27:22 as a mortar. It can be a hollow in the ground or in the jawbone; the Greek has the pit. En-hakkore, spring of the caller, is named for what he did in v18: va-yiqra, he called.

chapters.title: Samson and Delilah
chapters.html:
Judges 16

Gaza

1Samson went to Gaza and saw a prostitute there, and he went in to her.

2It was told to the Gazites, "Samson has come here." They surrounded the place and lay in wait for him all night at the city gate. They kept quiet all night, saying, "Let us wait until the light of morning; then we will kill him."

3Samson lay until midnight. At midnight he rose and took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two posts, pulled them up with the bar, put them on his shoulders and carried them to the top of the hill that faces Hebron.

Delilah

4And it came to pass afterward that he loved a woman in the Valley of Sorek, whose name was Delilah.

5The lords of the Philistines came up to her and said to her, "Coax him and see where his great strength lies, and by what means we can overpower him, so that we may bind him to subdue him. Then each of us will give you eleven hundred pieces of silver."

6Delilah said to Samson, "Please tell me where your great strength lies, and how you could be bound so that one could subdue you."

7Samson said to her, "If they bind me with seven fresh bowstrings that have not dried, I will become weak and be like any other man."

8The lords of the Philistines brought her seven fresh bowstrings that had not dried, and she bound him with them.

9The men lying in wait were sitting in an inner room. She said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He snapped the bowstrings as a thread of tow snaps when it touches fire. So the secret of his strength was not known.

10Delilah said to Samson, "You have mocked me and told me lies. Now please tell me how you could be bound."

11He said to her, "If they bind me with new ropes that have never been used for work, I will become weak and be like any other man."

12Delilah took new ropes and bound him with them and said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" The men lying in wait were sitting in the inner room. He snapped them off his arms like thread.

13Delilah said to Samson, "Until now you have mocked me and told me lies. Tell me how you could be bound." He said to her, "If you weave the seven locks of my head into the web and fasten it with the pin, I will become weak and be like any other man."

14She fastened it with the pin and said to him, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He woke from his sleep and pulled up the pin, the loom and the web.

15She said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? Three times you have mocked me and have not told me where your great strength lies."

16Because she pressed him hard with her words day after day and urged him, he was worn out to the point of death.

17He told her all his heart and said to her, "No razor has ever gone up on my head, for I have been a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become weak and be like anyone else."

18Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart. She sent and called the lords of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart." Then the lords of the Philistines came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.

19She lulled him to sleep on her knees and called a man and had him shave off the seven locks of his head. Then she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.

20She said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He woke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had left him.

The Prison

21The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes and brought him down to Gaza. They bound him with bronze shackles, and he was a grinder in the prison.

22But the hair of his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.

Dagon's House

23The lords of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice. They said, "Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."

24When the people saw him, they praised their god, for they said, "Our god has given our enemy into our hand, the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain."

25When their hearts were merry, they said, "Call Samson, and let him entertain us." They called Samson out of the prison, and he entertained them. They made him stand between the pillars.

26Samson said to the young man who held his hand, "Let me feel the pillars that support the house, so that I may lean on them."

27The house was full of men and women, and all the lords of the Philistines were there, and on the roof about three thousand men and women, watching while Samson entertained them.

28Samson called to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, just this once, O God, that with one act of revenge I may take revenge on the Philistines for my two eyes."

29Samson took hold of the two middle pillars on which the house rested, and braced himself against them, one with his right hand and one with his left.

30Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines." He pushed with all his strength, and the house fell on the lords and on all the people in it. So the dead whom he killed at his death were more than those he had killed in his life.

31His brothers and all his family went down and took him and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had judged Israel twenty years.

Notes

  • vv1, 4 "a prostitute… a woman in the Valley of Sorek" — ishah zonah, the words used of Rahab (Joshua 2:1). Delilah is not called a Philistine or anything else: the text gives her a name and a valley, and says only that Samson loved her. The Philistine lords come to her, and she does what they ask.

  • v5 "eleven hundred pieces of silver" — each of the lords offers this sum, and there are five (3:3). The same sum, eleven hundred pieces of silver, is what Micah takes from his mother in 17:2, at the start of the next story. Coax, patti, is the verb the Philistines used on Samson's wife in 14:15.

  • vv7, 11, 17 "I will become weak and be like any other man" — the same words in all three answers. The first two are false; the third is true and adds the reason.

  • v13 "into the web and fasten it with the pin, I will become weak…" — the Hebrew of v13 stops at with the web. It gives no pin and no result, though v14 says she fastened it with the pin and vv7 and 11 both give a result. The Greek fills both gaps: and drive it with the peg into the wall, and I shall be, like one of men, weak. The text follows the Greek for the pin and the result; into the wall is not in v14 and is left out.

  • v16 "worn out to the point of death" — va-tiqtsar nafsho la-mut, his soul grew short, the idiom used of the people in Numbers 21:4 and of the LORD in 10:16 (He could bear the misery of Israel no longer). Delilah wears Samson out as Israel's misery wore out God.

  • v17 "No razor has ever gone up on my head" — morah, as in 13:5, the words of the messenger before he was born. The hair is the mark of the Nazirite vow (Numbers 6:5, he shall let the locks of the hair of his head grow long), and he tells her that the vow is from my mother's womb, not one he took.

  • vv19–20 "his strength left him… the LORD had left him" — the same verb, sur, both times: va-yasar kocho me'alav in v19 and YHWH sar me'alav in v20. He wakes and does not know which has gone.

  • v21 "gouged out his eyes" — the man who saw a woman in Timnah (14:1) and one in Gaza (16:1), and for whom Timnah was right in my eyes (14:3, 7), loses his eyes in Gaza, the town where he first went in to a prostitute.

  • v25 "he entertained them" — va-yetsacheq, from tsachaq, to laugh, to play, the root of Isaac's name. The Greek has he played, and adds that they struck him.

  • v28 "for my two eyes" — Samson's second prayer, after the one at Lehi (15:18), asks for one act of revenge for two eyes. Israel is not mentioned; the promise of 13:5, he shall begin to save Israel, is not spoken by him here.

She said to him, "How can you say, 'I love you,' when your heart is not with me? Three times you have mocked me and have not told me where your great strength lies."
Because she pressed him hard with her words day after day and urged him, he was worn out to the point of death.

He told her all his heart and said to her, "No razor has ever gone up on my head, for I have been a Nazirite of God from my mother's womb. If I am shaved, my strength will leave me, and I will become weak and be like anyone else."

Delilah saw that he had told her all his heart. She sent and called the lords of the Philistines, saying, "Come up this once, for he has told me all his heart." Then the lords of the Philistines came up to her and brought the silver in their hands.
She lulled him to sleep on her knees and called a man and had him shave off the seven locks of his head. Then she began to subdue him, and his strength left him.
She said, "The Philistines are upon you, Samson!" He woke from his sleep and said, "I will go out as at other times and shake myself free." But he did not know that the LORD had left him.

The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes and brought him down to Gaza. They bound him with bronze shackles, and he was a grinder in the prison.
But the hair of his head began to grow again after it had been shaved.

The lords of the Philistines gathered to offer a great sacrifice to Dagon their god and to rejoice. They said, "Our god has given Samson our enemy into our hand."
When the people saw him, they praised their god, for they said, "Our god has given our enemy into our hand, the one who laid waste our land and multiplied our slain."

Samson called to the LORD and said, "Lord GOD, remember me, please, and strengthen me, please, just this once, O God, that with one act of revenge I may take revenge on the Philistines for my two eyes."

Samson said, "Let me die with the Philistines." He pushed with all his strength, and the house fell on the lords and on all the people in it. So the dead whom he killed at his death were more than those he had killed in his life.
His brothers and all his family went down and took him and brought him up and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol in the tomb of Manoah his father. He had judged Israel twenty years.

chapters.title: Micah's Idol and His Levite
chapters.html:
Judges 17

The Silver

1There was a man of the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Micah.

2He said to his mother, "The eleven hundred pieces of silver that were taken from you, about which you uttered a curse and also spoke it in my hearing — the silver is with me. I took it." His mother said, "Blessed be my son by the LORD."

3He gave the eleven hundred pieces of silver back to his mother, and his mother said, "I solemnly consecrate the silver to the LORD from my hand for my son, to make a carved image and a cast image. So now I will give it back to you."

4When he gave the silver back to his mother, his mother took two hundred pieces of silver and gave it to the silversmith, and he made it into a carved image and a cast image, and it was in the house of Micah.

5The man Micah had a house of God. He made an ephod and household gods, and ordained one of his sons, who became his priest.

6In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

The Levite

7There was a young man from Bethlehem in Judah, of the clan of Judah. He was a Levite, and he was living there as a guest.

8The man left the town of Bethlehem in Judah to live as a guest wherever he could find a place. He came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, as he went on his way.

9Micah said to him, "Where do you come from?" He said to him, "I am a Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to live as a guest wherever I can find a place."

10Micah said to him, "Stay with me, and be a father and a priest to me, and I will give you ten pieces of silver a year, a set of clothes and your food." So the Levite went in.

11The Levite agreed to stay with the man, and the young man became to him like one of his sons.

12Micah ordained the Levite, and the young man became his priest, and he was in the house of Micah.

13Micah said, "Now I know that the LORD will do me good, because I have a Levite as my priest."

Notes

  • vv1, 5 "Micah" — v1 spells his name in full, Mikhayehu, who is like the LORD?, and from v5 on it is the short form, Mikhah. The man whose name asks who is like the LORD? makes an image of Him.

  • v2 "you uttered a curse" — alit, from alah, an oath with a curse attached. Micah confesses because his mother cursed the thief, and she answers with a blessing to cancel it. The written text has ve-atti, the reading tradition ve-at, and you; the meaning is the same.

  • v3 "I solemnly consecrate the silver to the LORD… to make a carved image and a cast image" — haqdesh hiqdashti, a doubled verb. The silver is given to the LORD for the very thing Deuteronomy 27:15 curses: Cursed is the man who makes a carved or cast image. She means it as devotion.

  • v4 "two hundred pieces of silver" — of the eleven hundred she had consecrated. The text gives both numbers and does not comment.

  • v5 "an ephod and household gods" — ephod u-terafim. Gideon made an ephod that became a snare (8:27); terafim are the household gods Rachel stole from Laban (Genesis 31:19). Ordained is va-yemalle et yad, filled the hand, the words of Exodus 28:41 for Aaron's sons.

  • v6 "everyone did what was right in his own eyes" — Moses warned against this in Deuteronomy 12:8: You shall not do as we are doing here today, each man whatever is right in his own eyes. The line returns at 21:25 and closes the book; Samson chose his wife the same way (14:3).

  • vv7–9 "living there as a guest" — ger, and to live as a guest, la-gur, twice more. A Levite has no land of his own (Joshua 13:14), and this one, of the clan of Judah, has no town either. 18:30 names the priest the Danites took from Micah as Jonathan son of Gershom, and Gershom is the name Moses gave his son because I have been a guest in a foreign land (Exodus 2:22).

  • v10 "be a father and a priest to me" — father is a title of respect for a priest or prophet. The price is ten pieces of silver a year. v11 says the opposite relation too: the young man became to him like one of his sons.

  • v13 "Now I know that the LORD will do me good" — Micah is sure of the LORD's favor because he has hired a Levite. Nothing in the chapter says the LORD agreed.

chapters.title: The Danites Take Laish
chapters.html:
Judges 18

The Scouts

1In those days there was no king in Israel. In those days the tribe of the Danites was seeking an inheritance to live in, for until that day no inheritance had fallen to them among the tribes of Israel.

2The sons of Dan sent five men from their clan, from their whole number, men of valor from Zorah and Eshtaol, to spy out the land and explore it. They said to them, "Go, explore the land." They came to the hill country of Ephraim, to the house of Micah, and spent the night there.

3When they were at the house of Micah, they recognized the voice of the young Levite, and they turned aside there and said to him, "Who brought you here? What are you doing in this place? What do you have here?"

4He said to them, "Micah did this and that for me, and he has hired me, and I have become his priest."

5They said to him, "Please inquire of God, so that we may know whether the journey we are on will succeed."

6The priest said to them, "Go in peace. The journey you are on is before the LORD."

7The five men went on and came to Laish. They saw the people who were in it living in security, in the manner of the Sidonians, quiet and unsuspecting. There was no one in the land who put them to shame in anything or held power over them. They were far from the Sidonians and had no dealings with anyone.

8They came to their brothers at Zorah and Eshtaol, and their brothers said to them, "What have you found?"

9They said, "Arise, let us go up against them, for we have seen the land, and it is very good. Will you sit still? Do not be slow to go and enter and take possession of the land.

10When you go, you will come to an unsuspecting people, and the land is spacious. God has given it into your hand, a place where there is no lack of anything that is on the earth."

Micah's Gods Taken

11Six hundred men of the clan of the Danites set out from there, from Zorah and Eshtaol, armed with weapons of war.

12They went up and camped at Kiriath-jearim in Judah. That is why that place is called Mahaneh-dan to this day; it is west of Kiriath-jearim.

13From there they passed on to the hill country of Ephraim and came to the house of Micah.

14Then the five men who had gone to spy out the land of Laish said to their brothers, "Do you know that in these houses there are an ephod, household gods, a carved image and a cast image? So now consider what you will do."

15They turned aside there and came to the house of the young Levite, at the house of Micah, and greeted him.

16The six hundred men of the sons of Dan, armed with their weapons of war, stood at the entrance of the gate.

17The five men who had gone to spy out the land went up and went in and took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods and the cast image, while the priest stood at the entrance of the gate with the six hundred men armed with weapons of war.

18When these went into Micah's house and took the carved image, the ephod, the household gods and the cast image, the priest said to them, "What are you doing?"

19They said to him, "Be quiet. Put your hand over your mouth and come with us, and be a father and a priest to us. Is it better for you to be priest to the house of one man, or to be priest to a tribe and a clan in Israel?"

20The priest's heart was glad. He took the ephod, the household gods and the carved image, and went in among the people.

21They turned and went, and put the little ones, the livestock and the goods in front of them.

22When they were a good way from the house of Micah, the men who were in the houses near Micah's house were called out, and they overtook the sons of Dan.

23They shouted to the sons of Dan, who turned around and said to Micah, "What is the matter with you, that you have called out your men?"

24He said, "You have taken my gods that I made, and the priest, and gone away. What more do I have? How can you say to me, 'What is the matter with you?'"

25The sons of Dan said to him, "Do not let your voice be heard among us, or angry men will fall on you, and you will lose your life and the lives of your household."

26Then the sons of Dan went on their way. When Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.

Laish Becomes Dan

27They took what Micah had made and the priest he had, and came to Laish, to a people quiet and unsuspecting, and struck them with the sword and burned the city with fire.

28There was no one to save them, because it was far from Sidon and they had no dealings with anyone. It was in the valley that belongs to Beth-rehob. They rebuilt the city and lived in it.

29They called the name of the city Dan, after the name of Dan their father, who was born to Israel. But the name of the city was formerly Laish.

30The sons of Dan set up the carved image for themselves, and Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh, he and his sons were priests to the tribe of the Danites until the day the land went into exile.

31So they set up Micah's carved image that he had made for themselves, all the days that the house of God was at Shiloh.

Notes

  • v1 "no inheritance had fallen to them" — Joshua 19:40–48 records Dan's lot and says the territory of the sons of Dan was lost to them (19:47); 1:34 says the Amorites pushed them into the hill country. They have land on paper and none in hand. This chapter tells at length the move to Laish that Joshua 19:47 gives in one verse.

  • v3 "they recognized the voice of the young Levite" — hikkiru et qol: they knew him, or knew his way of speaking; the Hebrew does not say which. Their three questions come one after another.

  • v6 "The journey you are on is before the LORD" — nokhach YHWH, in front of the LORD. The words can mean that the LORD approves the journey or only that He sees it. The priest gives an answer that will please whoever hears it.

  • vv7, 10, 27 "quiet and unsuspecting" — shoqet u-voteach, said three times of Laish. The people of Laish are far from the Sidonians and have no allies; that is what makes them an easy target. No one who put them to shame… or held power over them is obscure in the Hebrew (yoresh etser), and the Greek is no clearer.

  • v9 "it is very good" — the report of Joshua and Caleb in Numbers 14:7, a very, very good land. There the spies urged Israel on against strong cities; here they urge an attack on a town with no defenders.

  • v12 "Mahaneh-dan" — camp of Dan, the place where the Spirit first stirred Samson (13:25).

  • vv14–20 the gods are taken — Micah's image, ephod and household gods are carried off by a tribe that asks the priest what he prefers, and the priest's heart was glad. Be a father and a priest to us (v19) are Micah's own words to him (17:10).

  • v24 "You have taken my gods that I made" — the chapter's plainest line. Micah calls them my gods and says he made them; what the prophets later mock (Isaiah 44:17) he says of himself.

  • v30 "Jonathan son of Gershom, son of Manasseh" — Moses' son was named Gershom (Exodus 2:22), and Manasseh, Mnshh, differs from Moses, Mshh, by one letter, n. The Hebrew and the Greek both read Manasseh, and the text follows them. Until the day the land went into exile reaches far past the book's own time.

  • v31 "all the days that the house of God was at Shiloh" — a second measure of the same time, and a pointed one: the true house of God stood at Shiloh (Joshua 18:1) while Dan kept Micah's image.

chapters.title: The Levite's Concubine
chapters.html:
Judges 19

Bethlehem

1And it came to pass in those days, when there was no king in Israel, that a Levite was living as a guest in the far parts of the hill country of Ephraim. He took for himself a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.

2His concubine whored against him, and she left him and went to her father's house at Bethlehem in Judah, and she was there some four months.

3Her husband rose and went after her, to speak to her heart and bring her back. His servant was with him, and a pair of donkeys. She brought him into her father's house, and when the girl's father saw him, he was glad to meet him.

4His father-in-law, the girl's father, kept him there, and he stayed with him three days. They ate and drank and spent the nights there.

5On the fourth day they rose early in the morning, and he got up to go. But the girl's father said to his son-in-law, "Refresh yourself with a bit of bread, and after that you may go."

6So the two of them sat down and ate and drank together, and the girl's father said to the man, "Please agree to stay the night, and let your heart be merry."

7The man got up to go, but his father-in-law pressed him, and he stayed there again for the night.

8He rose early in the morning on the fifth day to go, and the girl's father said, "Please refresh yourself, and wait until the day wears on." So the two of them ate.

9When the man got up to go, he and his concubine and his servant, his father-in-law, the girl's father, said to him, "The day has worn on toward evening. Please stay the night. The day is coming to an end; stay here and let your heart be merry. Tomorrow you can rise early for your journey and go home to your tent."

Gibeah

10But the man would not stay the night. He rose and went, and came as far as opposite Jebus, that is, Jerusalem. He had with him a pair of saddled donkeys, and his concubine was with him.

11When they were near Jebus, the day was far spent, and the servant said to his master, "Come, let us turn aside to this city of the Jebusites and spend the night in it."

12His master said to him, "We will not turn aside into a city of foreigners who are not of the sons of Israel. We will go on to Gibeah."

13He said to his servant, "Come, let us draw near to one of these places and spend the night at Gibeah or at Ramah."

14So they passed on and went their way, and the sun went down on them near Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin.

15They turned aside there to go in and spend the night at Gibeah. He went in and sat down in the open square of the city, but no one took them into his house for the night.

16Then an old man came in from his work in the field at evening. The man was from the hill country of Ephraim, and he was living as a guest in Gibeah; the men of the place were Benjaminites.

17He lifted up his eyes and saw the traveler in the open square of the city, and the old man said, "Where are you going, and where do you come from?"

18He said to him, "We are passing from Bethlehem in Judah to the far parts of the hill country of Ephraim. I am from there. I went to Bethlehem in Judah, and I am going to the house of the LORD, but no one takes me into his house.

19We have straw and fodder for our donkeys, and bread and wine for me and your maidservant and for the young man with your servants. We lack nothing."

20The old man said, "Peace to you. Let all your needs be on me; only do not spend the night in the square."

21He brought him into his house and gave the donkeys fodder. They washed their feet and ate and drank.

The Night

22While they were making their hearts merry, the men of the city, worthless men, surrounded the house and beat on the door. They said to the old man, the master of the house, "Bring out the man who came into your house, so that we may know him."

23The man, the master of the house, went out to them and said to them, "No, my brothers, please do not do evil. Since this man has come into my house, do not do this outrage.

24Here are my virgin daughter and his concubine. Let me bring them out now. Violate them and do with them what is good in your eyes, but to this man do not do this outrageous thing."

25But the men would not listen to him. So the Levite seized his concubine and put her out to them, and they knew her and abused her all night until morning, and let her go as the dawn came up.

26The woman came at the turning of the morning and fell down at the entrance of the man's house where her master was, until it was light.

27Her master rose in the morning, opened the doors of the house and went out to go on his way. The woman, his concubine, was lying at the entrance of the house, with her hands on the threshold.

28He said to her, "Get up, let us go." But there was no answer. Then he put her on the donkey, and the man rose and went to his place.

29When he came to his house, he took the knife, seized his concubine and cut her limb by limb into twelve pieces, and sent her throughout all the territory of Israel.

30And it would come to pass that everyone who saw it would say, "Nothing like this has happened or been seen from the day the sons of Israel came up from the land of Egypt until this day. Consider it, take counsel and speak."

Notes

  • v2 "His concubine whored against him" — va-tizneh alav. Leaving him for her father's house is an odd act for an unfaithful wife, and the Greek does not have the verb at all: his concubine went away from him. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • v3 "to speak to her heart" — ledabber al libbah, the words used of Shechem to Dinah (Genesis 34:3) and of Joseph to his brothers (50:21): to speak tenderly, to win back. Nothing in the chapter shows him doing it.

  • vv4–9 the father's hospitality — five days of eat and drink… let your heart be merry. The delay puts the Levite on the road late on the fifth day, and the chapter turns on where he will spend the night. Refresh yourself with a bit of bread is se'ad libbekha pat lechem, Abraham's offer to his guests in Genesis 18:5.

  • v12 "a city of foreigners who are not of the sons of Israel" — Jebus is passed by for safety, and Gibeah, a town of Benjamin, is chosen. What follows happens in Israel.

  • v18 "I am going to the house of the LORD" — the Greek has I am going to my house. The Levite's house is in the hill country of Ephraim (v1), and so is Shiloh, where the house of God stood (18:31); either reading fits the road he is on. The text follows the Hebrew.

  • vv22–24 "so that we may know him" — the scene repeats Sodom almost word for word: the house surrounded (Genesis 19:4), Bring out… that we may know (19:5), my brothers, do not do evil (19:7), and a host who offers the women instead, do with them what is good in your eyes (19:8). At Sodom the messengers pulled Lot inside and struck the men blind. Here no one comes.

  • vv23–24 "this outrage" — nevalah, the word for what Shechem did to Dinah, an outrage in Israel (Genesis 34:7).

  • v28 "But there was no answer" — the Hebrew does not say whether she is dead. The Greek adds for she was dead.

  • v29 "the knife… cut her limb by limb" — ha-ma'akhelet, the knife Abraham took to slaughter his son (Genesis 22:10), and va-yenatcheha, the verb for cutting a burnt offering into pieces (Leviticus 1:6, 12). Twelve pieces, one for each tribe. Saul will do the same with a pair of oxen, va-yenatchehu… va-yeshallach be-khol gevul Yisra'el, the same words (1 Samuel 11:7).

  • v30 "Consider it, take counsel and speak" — the chapter ends with a call to the tribes, and chapter 20 is their answer.

chapters.title: War Against Benjamin
chapters.html:
Judges 20

The Assembly at Mizpah

1Then all the sons of Israel came out, from Dan to Beersheba and the land of Gilead, and the congregation assembled as one man to the LORD at Mizpah.

2The leaders of all the people, of all the tribes of Israel, presented themselves in the assembly of the people of God, four hundred thousand foot soldiers who drew the sword.

3The sons of Benjamin heard that the sons of Israel had gone up to Mizpah. The sons of Israel said, "Tell us, how did this evil happen?"

4The Levite, the husband of the murdered woman, answered and said, "I came to Gibeah, which belongs to Benjamin, I and my concubine, to spend the night.

5The lords of Gibeah rose against me and surrounded the house against me by night. They meant to kill me, and they violated my concubine, and she died.

6I took my concubine and cut her in pieces and sent her throughout all the country of Israel's inheritance, because they have committed lewdness and outrage in Israel.

7All of you are sons of Israel. Give your word and counsel here."

8All the people rose as one man, saying, "None of us will go to his tent, and none of us will turn back to his house.

9And now this is what we will do to Gibeah: we will go up against it by lot.

10We will take ten men of a hundred from all the tribes of Israel, and a hundred of a thousand, and a thousand of ten thousand, to bring provisions for the people, so that when they come to Gibeah of Benjamin they may do to it for all the outrage it has committed in Israel."

11So all the men of Israel gathered against the city, united as one man.

Benjamin Refuses

12The tribes of Israel sent men through all the tribe of Benjamin, saying, "What is this evil that has happened among you?

13And now give up the men, the worthless men in Gibeah, so that we may put them to death and purge the evil from Israel." But the sons of Benjamin would not listen to the voice of their brothers, the sons of Israel.

14The sons of Benjamin gathered from the cities to Gibeah to go out to battle against the sons of Israel.

15On that day the sons of Benjamin mustered from the cities twenty-six thousand men who drew the sword, besides the inhabitants of Gibeah, who mustered seven hundred chosen men.

16Among all these people were seven hundred chosen men who were left-handed; every one could sling a stone at a hair and not miss.

17The men of Israel, apart from Benjamin, mustered four hundred thousand men who drew the sword; all of these were men of war.

Two Defeats

18They rose and went up to Bethel and inquired of God. The sons of Israel said, "Who shall go up first for us to battle against the sons of Benjamin?" The LORD said, "Judah first."

19The sons of Israel rose in the morning and camped against Gibeah.

20The men of Israel went out to battle against Benjamin, and the men of Israel drew up for battle against them at Gibeah.

21The sons of Benjamin came out of Gibeah and struck down twenty-two thousand men of Israel to the ground that day.

22But the people, the men of Israel, took courage and again drew up for battle in the place where they had drawn up on the first day.

23The sons of Israel went up and wept before the LORD until evening, and they inquired of the LORD, saying, "Shall we again go near to battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother?" The LORD said, "Go up against him."

24So the sons of Israel came near against the sons of Benjamin on the second day.

25Benjamin went out against them from Gibeah on the second day and struck down eighteen thousand more of the sons of Israel to the ground; all of these drew the sword.

26Then all the sons of Israel, the whole people, went up and came to Bethel and wept. They sat there before the LORD and fasted that day until evening, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings before the LORD.

27The sons of Israel inquired of the LORD — the ark of the covenant of God was there in those days,

28and Phinehas son of Eleazar, son of Aaron, stood before it in those days — saying, "Shall I go out once more to battle against the sons of Benjamin my brother, or shall I stop?" The LORD said, "Go up, for tomorrow I will give him into your hand."

The Ambush

29So Israel set men in ambush all around Gibeah.

30The sons of Israel went up against the sons of Benjamin on the third day and drew up against Gibeah as at the other times.

31The sons of Benjamin went out against the people and were drawn away from the city. As at the other times, they began to strike down some of the people on the highways, one of which goes up to Bethel and the other to Gibeah in the open country, about thirty men of Israel.

32The sons of Benjamin said, "They are being struck down before us as at first." But the sons of Israel said, "Let us flee and draw them away from the city to the highways."

33All the men of Israel rose from their place and drew up at Baal-tamar, and the men of Israel in ambush burst out of their place, from the open ground of Geba.

34Ten thousand chosen men from all Israel came against Gibeah, and the battle was hard, but the Benjaminites did not know that disaster was close upon them.

35The LORD struck Benjamin before Israel, and the sons of Israel destroyed twenty-five thousand one hundred men of Benjamin that day; all of these drew the sword.

36The sons of Benjamin saw that they were struck down. The men of Israel had given ground to Benjamin, because they trusted the ambush they had set against Gibeah.

37The men in ambush hurried and rushed upon Gibeah; the ambush spread out and struck the whole city with the sword.

38Now the appointed signal between the men of Israel and the men in ambush was that they should make a great cloud of smoke rise up from the city.

39When the men of Israel turned in the battle, Benjamin had begun to strike down about thirty of the men of Israel, for they said, "They are surely struck down before us, as in the first battle."

40But the signal began to rise from the city, a column of smoke, and Benjamin looked behind them, and the whole city was going up to heaven.

41Then the men of Israel turned, and the men of Benjamin were terrified, for they saw that disaster had come upon them.

42They turned before the men of Israel toward the way of the wilderness, but the battle overtook them, and those who came out of the cities destroyed them in the middle of them.

43They surrounded Benjamin, pursued them and trod them down at their resting place, as far as opposite Gibeah toward the sunrise.

44Eighteen thousand men of Benjamin fell; all of these were men of valor.

45They turned and fled toward the wilderness to the Rock of Rimmon, and Israel gleaned five thousand men of them on the highways, and pursued them hard as far as Gidom and struck down two thousand men of them.

46So all who fell of Benjamin that day were twenty-five thousand men who drew the sword; all of these were men of valor.

47But six hundred men turned and fled toward the wilderness to the Rock of Rimmon, and they stayed at the Rock of Rimmon four months.

48The men of Israel turned back against the sons of Benjamin and struck them with the sword, the whole city, people and animals, everything that was found. All the cities that were found they also set on fire.

  • v1 "from Dan to Beersheba" — the first use of the phrase for the whole land, north to south. Dan is the city just founded in 18:29. As one man returns in vv8 and 11: Israel is never so united in the book as against one of its own tribes.

  • vv4–6 the Levite's account — he says the men of Gibeah meant to kill me (19:22 says they asked to know him), and he does not say that he put his concubine out to them himself (19:25). Lewdness and outrage, zimmah u-nevalah: nevalah is the old man's word in 19:23.

  • v13 "purge the evil from Israel" — the formula of Deuteronomy, So you shall purge the evil from among you (13:5, 17:7). Benjamin refuses to give up the guilty, and the whole tribe is drawn in.

  • vv15–16 the numbers of Benjamin — the Hebrew has 26,000 besides 700 of Gibeah; v35 counts 25,100 dead, v46 about 25,000, and v47 leaves 600. The totals do not agree exactly, and the Greek of v15 has 23,000. The text gives the Hebrew figures as they stand.

  • v16 "left-handed… and not miss" — itter yad-yemino, the phrase used of Ehud the Benjaminite (3:15). Not miss is lo yachati, from chata, to miss the mark, the ordinary Hebrew word for sin. The Greek has ambidextrous.

  • v18 "Who shall go up first… Judah first" — the question and answer of 1:1–2, where the enemy was the Canaanites. Now the enemy is Benjamin.

  • vv27–28 "the ark… Phinehas son of Eleazar" — the priest who led the embassy of Joshua 22 is still serving. His presence places this story early in the time of the judges, though the book tells it last.

  • vv29–41 the ambush — the plan that took Ai (Joshua 8): a feigned flight, the enemy drawn from the city, the ambush breaking in, and smoke that tells the fleeing side the city is lost (the smoke of the city was going up to the heavens, Joshua 8:20). Israel now uses it on Israel.

  • v40 "the whole city was going up to heaven" — kelil ha-ir, the city whole, the word of Deuteronomy 13:16 for a town under the ban burned whole, to the LORD your God.

  • vv43, 45 "at their resting place… gleaned" — menuchah can be resting place or a place name, Menuhah; the Greek has from Noua. Va-ye'olleluhu, they gleaned them, is the word for picking over a harvested field.

chapters.title: Wives for Benjamin
chapters.html:
Judges 21

The Oath at Mizpah

1The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah, "None of us shall give his daughter to Benjamin as a wife."

2The people came to Bethel and sat there before God until evening, and they lifted up their voices and wept bitterly.

3They said, "LORD, God of Israel, why has this happened in Israel, that today one tribe should be missing from Israel?"

4The next day the people rose early and built an altar there, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings.

5The sons of Israel said, "Who from all the tribes of Israel did not come up in the assembly to the LORD?" For they had taken a great oath concerning anyone who did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah: "He shall surely be put to death."

6The sons of Israel were sorry for Benjamin their brother and said, "Today one tribe is cut off from Israel.

7What shall we do for wives for those who are left, since we have sworn by the LORD not to give them any of our daughters as wives?"

Jabesh-gilead

8They said, "Which one of the tribes of Israel did not come up to the LORD at Mizpah?" No one had come to the camp from Jabesh-gilead, to the assembly.

9When the people were counted, not one of the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead was there.

10So the congregation sent twelve thousand of the men of valor there and commanded them, "Go and strike the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead with the sword, with the women and the little ones.

11This is what you shall do: every male, and every woman who has lain with a male, you shall devote to destruction."

12Among the inhabitants of Jabesh-gilead they found four hundred young virgins who had not known a man by lying with a male, and they brought them to the camp at Shiloh, which is in the land of Canaan.

13Then the whole congregation sent word and spoke to the sons of Benjamin who were at the Rock of Rimmon, and proclaimed peace to them.

14Benjamin came back at that time, and they gave them the women whom they had kept alive of the women of Jabesh-gilead. But there were not enough for them.

The Daughters of Shiloh

15The people were sorry for Benjamin, because the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel.

16The elders of the congregation said, "What shall we do for wives for those who are left, since the women of Benjamin have been destroyed?"

17They said, "There must be an inheritance for the survivors of Benjamin, so that a tribe is not wiped out from Israel.

18But we cannot give them wives from our daughters, for the sons of Israel have sworn, 'Cursed be anyone who gives a wife to Benjamin.'"

19They said, "There is the feast of the LORD at Shiloh year by year, which is north of Bethel, on the east of the highway that goes up from Bethel to Shechem, and south of Lebonah."

20They commanded the sons of Benjamin, "Go and lie in wait in the vineyards,

21and watch. When the daughters of Shiloh come out to dance in the dances, come out of the vineyards and each of you seize a wife for himself from the daughters of Shiloh, and go to the land of Benjamin.

22And it shall come to pass, when their fathers or their brothers come to complain to us, that we will say to them, 'Be gracious to us about them, because we did not take a wife for each man in the war, and you did not give them to them yourselves; otherwise you would now be guilty.'"

23The sons of Benjamin did so, and took wives according to their number from the dancers whom they carried off. Then they went and returned to their inheritance, rebuilt the cities and lived in them.

24The sons of Israel went from there at that time, each to his tribe and his clan, and each went out from there to his inheritance.

25In those days there was no king in Israel; everyone did what was right in his own eyes.

Notes

  • v1 "The men of Israel had sworn at Mizpah" — the oath was not told in chapter 20. It comes to light only now, when it has become a problem. A second oath follows in v5, and the chapter is spent getting around both without breaking either in words.

  • v3 "why has this happened in Israel" — the question is put to the LORD, and v15 answers it on His behalf: the LORD had made a breach in the tribes of Israel. The people who fought the war now speak of it as something done to them.

  • v6 "were sorry for Benjamin their brother" — va-yinnachamu, the verb the book used of the LORD being moved to pity (2:18). Cut off, nigda, is the verb for hewing down a tree or an Asherah (Deuteronomy 7:5).

  • vv10–12 Jabesh-gilead — the order repeats Moses' command against Midian almost word for word: kill every woman who has known a man by lying with a male… the girls who have not known a man by lying with a male, keep alive (Numbers 31:17–18). Israel now gives that order against a town of Israel. Jabesh-gilead will be the town Saul rescues first (1 Samuel 11:1) and the town that buries him (1 Samuel 31:11).

  • v14 "there were not enough for them" — four hundred women for six hundred men (20:47).

  • v19 "the feast of the LORD at Shiloh year by year" — the house of God is at Shiloh (18:31), yet the directions to it are given at length as if the place needed finding. Year by year, mi-yamim yamimah, is the phrase for Elkanah's yearly journey to Shiloh in 1 Samuel 1:3 and for the yearly lament for Jephthah's daughter (11:40).

  • v21 "seize a wife" — chataf, to snatch, to catch as prey. Their fathers did not give the daughters of Shiloh, so the oath of v1 is kept.

  • v22 "Be gracious to us about them… otherwise you would now be guilty" — the plan for answering the fathers is compressed in the Hebrew and hard to follow. The sense is that since the fathers did not give their daughters, they have not broken the oath; the Greek is no clearer.

  • v23 "whom they carried off" — gazalu, the word for robbery.

  • v25 "In those days there was no king in Israel" — the line of 17:6, 18:1 and 19:1, and the full refrain of 17:6 ends the book. The last five chapters show what everyone did what was right in his own eyes looks like, and the book closes on the words without comment.
